content: This medication should be taken orally, either with or without food, as directed by your doctor. Typically, it is taken once daily, but in some cases, it may be prescribed twice weekly. It is crucial to follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking this medication, along with any other tuberculosis (TB) medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve before completing the course. Common side effects may include headache, loss of appetite, upset stomach, nausea, or vomiting. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Before starting ethambutol, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ethambutol may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, alcohol consumption may increase the risk of liver disease. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. While it passes into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. However, if you have HIV, breastfeeding may transmit the virus to your baby. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While taking this medication, you may need to undergo laboratory and medical tests, such as sputum tests, eye and vision exams, kidney and liver function tests, and complete blood counts. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
